summary: Group all odd-indexed nodes followed by all even-indexed nodes in place.
mainInsight: Keep two pointers, odd (starting at head) and even (starting at head.next), and remember even_head. Repeatedly link odd.next = even.next, advance odd, then even.next = odd.next and advance even. Finally append the even list: odd.next = even_head.

cards.answer: Rewire with an odd pointer and an even pointer to build two chains, then attach the even chain after the odd chain. Clue: Nodes must be regrouped by the parity of their position with the relative order kept, so build an odd chain and an even chain with two pointers and join them.

cards.explanation: Each node only needs its next pointer redirected to the node two steps ahead, which splits the list into the two chains without moving values.

incorrectOptionExplanations.A slow pointer and a fast pointer, both: Those find the middle, not the odd/even split.
incorrectOptionExplanations.A dummy node and one previous pointer, a: That does not hold the even list head.

promptVariants: Why is the loop condition `even and even.next`?
What happens at the end of the list?
cards.answer: Each iteration reads even.next and then odd.next, so both even and even.next must exist. When it fails, odd points to the last odd node, so attaching even_head there completes the list.
keyPoints: Odd pointer is the last odd node
cards.explanation: Handles odd and even length lists.
